title: Manicouagan Reservoir – The Eye of Quebec

beats.text: Type these coordinates into a satellite map, and you'll find something strange in central Quebec.
A perfect circular lake, seventy kilometers wide, rings like an eye from space.
Scientists call it the eye of Quebec, but what made such a giant ring?
Could a meteor have carved this massive crater?
About two hundred fourteen million years ago, a meteor five kilometers across struck here.
The impact shattered rock, forming a multi-ring basin about one hundred kilometers across.
Water filled the basin, a lake that hides an island crowned by a nine-hundred-fifty meter peak.
So the strange eye you saw is a 214 million year old impact crater.
Follow for more places you can see from space.

description: Manicouagan Reservoir is a seventy‑kilometer wide annular lake in central Quebec, formed by a meteor impact two hundred fourteen million years ago. The impact created a multi‑ring basin about one hundred kilometers across, with a central island plateau topped by Mount Babel. Imagery: Esri, Maxar, Earthstar Geographics.
